key_insight: A cascaded multi-stage LLM pipeline produces grounded, attribution-rich answers to patient questions over EHRs, improving reliability and interpretability of clinical QA.
problem_solved: Enables grounded question answering over electronic health records (ArchEHR-QA), addressing patient confusion and reducing unverified or hallucinated responses from LLMs when interpreting complex clinical data.
method: Cascaded pipeline that separates retrieval, context assembly, and answer generation to ensure relevant evidence is identified before reasoning.
Ranking and context-conditioning steps filter and organize EHR snippets so the LLM generates answers anchored to source text with explicit citations or provenance.
Final verification/attribution stage enforces grounding and mitigates hallucination, producing concise, patient-facing responses linked to original records.
impact: Provides a practical blueprint for building trustworthy, explainable clinical QA systems: improves safety and user trust by combining retrieval and LLM reasoning while preserving provenance. Useful for AI/ML teams deploying patient-facing EHR assistants or clinical decision-support tools.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing stages: Retrieval → Rerank/Context Assembly → LLM Answering → Attribution/Verification
Example patient Q&A card: question, concise answer, and highlighted source snippets with citations
Bar chart or table comparing grounded-answer accuracy and hallucination rates versus a non-cascaded baseline
Icons representing goals: magnifier (retrieval), document with quote (grounding), shield/checkmark (safety/verification)
paper_title: HealthNLP_Retrievers at ArchEHR-QA 2026: Cascaded LLM Pipeline for Grounded Clinical Question Answering
paper_authors: Md Biplob Hosen, Md Alomgeer Hussein, Md Akmol Masud, Omar Faruque, Tera L Reynolds
